behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the TRAIN split only. Scan each user's consecutive interactions, count item->item transitions, keep the top M=20 successors S(i) per item (ties by item id) in a cached sparse matrix. Per level, euc_l(j) = argmin_k ||z_j^l - v_k|| over all 24556 training items, recomputed identically at each epoch from the current codebook; a_ik = (1/|S(i)|) * sum_{j in S(i)} 1[euc_l(j)=k] in [0,1]. Curvature profile: nodes are the K_l codes used at level l, edge weight w_kk' = number of training transitions u->v with euc_l(u)=k and euc_l(v)=k'; Ollivier-Ricci curvature kappa(k,k') = 1 - W1(m_k, m_k')/d_G(k,k') with m_k = 0.5*delta_k + 0.5*sum_k' (w_kk'/deg k) delta_k' and exact OT on at most 256 nodes; kappa_l = transition-weighted edge mean; 200 member-shuffles that preserve community sizes give mu_l, sigma_l; kappa_hat_l = clip((kappa_l-mu_l)/max(sigma_l,1e-6), -2, 2); delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l' kappa_hat_l'. Recomputed every 50 epochs under no_grad.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

Validation and test interactions are never tokenised for SID construction, never counted in w_kk', and never used for a_ik or u_k. The curvature profile is computed offline before launch, written to a file, and read identically by every rank, so no validation pass can influence the SID; the export uses only train-fitted codebooks.

behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item transitions (u -> v, v the next interaction in the same training sequence), aggregated into a code-level transition graph; the quantity the mechanism consumes is the Ollivier curvature of that quotient graph, i.e. how much the successor distributions of two codes overlap.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: Enumerated from TRAINING split interactions only, in order, giving a multiset `T_train` of directed pairs (u,v). For each level l each pair is mapped to `(A_l[u], A_l[v])` using the last-synced detached memberships, EMA-updated every 20 epochs from the current argmax assignment. Count, symmetrise (`W = N + N^T`), row-normalise, compute per-edge Ollivier curvature with an entropic W1 over the quotient graph, aggregate per node by W-weighted mean, standardise against a member-shuffle null (8 shuffles), clip to +-3 sigma. No gradient flows through any of it; it is a schedule producing 3 x 256 scalars every 20 epochs.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition set is built exclusively from training-split sequences. Validation and test sequences are never enumerated, never mapped to codes, never enter the quotient graph or the null. The null shuffles only training memberships, so `sigma` is a property of the training split's own size and degree distribution. The 4096-item probe used by the alpha safeguard is drawn from training items only. The exported SID is a deterministic function of the training-only code table, training-only transition graph and training memberships, and since the protocol has no early stopping there is no validation signal that could select an epoch. Nothing in the assignment consumes a validation or test interaction.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: The standardised, code-local mean Ollivier-Ricci curvature s_e of the directed training item-transition graph restricted to the items each codeword served in the previous epoch; equivalently a per-code measure of how tree-like (branching, negative curvature) versus clique-like (redundant, positive curvature) the successor structure of that code's cell is.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the TRAINING split only: for each training user sequence, consecutive (i_t, i_t+1) pairs increment n_ij; the item graph has the 24556 training items as nodes and the observed directed pairs as edges; the lazy random-walk measure m_i = 0.5 delta_i + 0.5 p_i is compared to m_j by entropic Wasserstein-1 with eps = 1/(2 max_out_degree), and kappa_OR(i,j) = 1 - W1/dist(i,j). Item curvature kappa_i is the out-edge mean; code curvature is the mean over the code's assigned items, taken from the previous epoch's assignments, standardised against R = 8 size-preserving member shuffles and clipped to +-3. Nothing in this path is differentiable and nothing in it is updated by backpropagation.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The graph, the measures and kappa_i are built exclusively from training-split sequences; the validation and test interactions are never read, never touched during encoding, and never used to fit the transition graph or the per-code means. The standardisation null is a member shuffle of TRAINING items among codes, so it carries no split information either. rho_l is measured from the run's own epoch-0 residuals on training batches. behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item-to-item transitions and user-interest branching extracted from training sequences, aggregated at each RQ level into a prefix-level quotient graph whose standardised Ollivier-Ricci curvature profile is the behaviour term.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training split only, over all training sequences, count directed pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) with immediate repeats suppressed, giving a sparse item transition matrix W (24556 x 24556). At recompute time, take the current DDP-synchronised encoder and codebooks, encode the 24556 training items once, assign prefixes 1..l-1, and sum W over prefix pairs to build the sparse quotient graph A_l (level 1 is the item graph itself). Compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature per edge (lazy random walk with standard 0.5 laziness, Wasserstein-1 via a sparse min-cost solve or Sinkhorn with a fixed small epsilon), and take the transition-count-weighted mean as kappa_raw,l. Null: B=10 replicates; for level 1 rewire W by degree-preserving stub matching; for levels 2,3 permute the item-to-prefix labels while preserving each prefix size, then recompute. z_l is the standardised deviation. Everything is computed with torch.no_grad and stored as a schedule tensor; it never enters the backward graph.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: W is built exclusively from training-split sequences; validation and test sequences are never read, and no validation or test item is added to the graph or to the prefix map used for curvature. The null shuffles permute only training items. The schedule uses only the training item universe and the current codebook, which itself is trained on the training split. The exported SID table is built from the training item universe only. No validation or test interaction, reward, or click can enter kappa_l or the residual operator, and the Stage3 protocol remains frozen and untouched.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: config flag behaviour_off sets a_ik = 0 for all pairs and delta_l = 0, so c_ik = 1 at every level; the cost is a uniform-curvature Poincaré distance and the capacity-frozen Sinkhorn is otherwise unchanged.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full C_ik = d_{c_l*exp(-a_ik)}(psi(z_i), psi(v_k)) with capacity-frozen Sinkhorn and straight-through gradient; this is the single trained arm, and no arm is trained with the switches off in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: config flag geometry_off sets C_ik = ||z_i^l - v_k||, the Euclidean limit; because the column capacities are exactly this assignment's own counts, the plan returns the Euclidean nearest-code assignment, a_ik has no channel, and the run is the plain RQ-VAE plus a no-op permutation.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAIN split only. Scan each user's consecutive interactions, count item->item transitions, keep the top M=20 successors S(i) per item (ties by item id) in a cached sparse matrix. Per level, euc_l(j) = argmin_k ||z_j^l - v_k|| over all 24556 training items, recomputed identically at each epoch from the current codebook; a_ik = (1/|S(i)|) * sum_{j in S(i)} 1[euc_l(j)=k] in [0,1]. Curvature profile: nodes are the K_l codes used at level l, edge weight w_kk' = number of training transitions u->v with euc_l(u)=k and euc_l(v)=k'; Ollivier-Ricci curvature kappa(k,k') = 1 - W1(m_k, m_k')/d_G(k,k') with m_k = 0.5*delta_k + 0.5*sum_k' (w_kk'/deg k) delta_k' and exact OT on at most 256 nodes; kappa_l = transition-weighted edge mean; 200 member-shuffles that preserve community sizes give mu_l, sigma_l; kappa_hat_l = clip((kappa_l-mu_l)/max(sigma_l,1e-6), -2, 2); delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l' kappa_hat_l'. Recomputed every 50 epochs under no_grad.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions from the training split, aggregated as each item's top-M successor set, plus the level-l community curvature of the training transition quotient graph.
ideas.cost_estimate: Added ~108M MAC per step at the frozen scale (B=1023, K=256, d=64, J=10: 3*B*K*d for the curved cost matrix, 3*B*K*d for the Euclidean capacity pass, 3*B*K*J for the ten Sinkhorn iterations), about 0.22 GFLOP per step, i.e. roughly 1.0-1.8x the ~120M MAC RQ-VAE step. Over 72,000 steps that is ~1.6e13 added FLOPs, about 10-40 min extra on four cards including launch overhead. The curvature schedule (60 recomputations x 3 levels x <=256-node exact ORC) costs under one minute. The 256-per-level codebooks are consistent with the frozen 247/7414/20223 support; if one level used 4096 codes its per-step cost would grow 16x.
ideas.coupling_equation: C_ik = d_{c_l * exp(-a_ik)}( psi(z_i^l), psi(v_k) ), with a_ik = (1/|S(i)|) * sum_{j in S(i)} 1[euc_l(j)=k] and c_l = exp(-delta_l/2).
ideas.coupling_path: a_ik (the codes of the item's training successors) sets the local curvature c_ik of the distance that prices item i against code k; that same distance forms the cost matrix of a transport whose marginals are frozen to the Euclidean counts, so the plan, the chosen code, the residual and the next level's assignment all depend jointly on the behaviour affinity and the curved metric. Removing behaviour makes c_ik uniform and removes the successor channel; removing geometry makes the cost Euclidean and the affinity has no channel at all, so the plan collapses to the Euclidean assignment.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If an item's level-l prefix should coincide with the level-l prefix its training successors already occupy, then letting curvature pull the assignment toward successor codes while capacity forbids any resolution loss should raise prefix sharing along transitions and lift Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 (from 0.055537), with the exported SID support unchanged and with 5-40% of level-1 codes permuted relative to the geometry-off assignment. It is worth keeping only if both the permutation fraction is non-trivial and recall moves.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer's assignment step at all three levels, and in the gradient that flows through the straight-through soft plan to the encoder and the codebook. Not in the code radius, not in the decoder, not in the latent scale.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball distance with Möbius addition and a per-pair negative sectional curvature -c_ik, where c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik) and c_l = clamp(exp(-delta_l/2), 0.25, 4.0) with c_0 = 1 dimensionless: d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-u) (+) v||_c). The curvature is fixed/scheduled, never trained.
ideas.key_change: Replaces the per-level nearest-code step by a curvature-field, capacity-frozen optimal-transport assignment in which each item-code pair carries its own Poincaré sectional curvature, fixed by the fraction of the item's training successors already sitting in that code's community.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every transition, successor set, community size, curvature value, null sample, capacity count and code table is built from training interactions and the training item universe only. Validation and test interactions are never tokenised for SID construction, never counted in w_kk', and never used for a_ik or u_k. The curvature profile is computed offline before launch, written to a file, and read identically by every rank, so no validation pass can influence the SID; the export uses only train-fitted codebooks.
ideas.motivation: The prior round proved that the curvature signal tracks SID quality (Spearman -0.20) but spent that signal on the per-level code radius rho_l, collapsing the codebook: exported support 2/13/56, collision rate 0.998, L1 positive/negative hit rates 0.982/0.980, Stage3 test_recall@10 0.041888 against 0.055537. Curvature and resolution were competing for the same scalar. The fix is to change the currency: curvature may decide WHICH item occupies WHICH code, never how much of the ball a code occupies.
ideas.novelty: Unlike CURVALLOC (curvature -> c_l and rho_l), BRad-RQ (rank/radial assignment by context entropy), CURVCTRL-SID (prefix score -> per-level temperature), poincare-frechet (curved codebook update), and unlike a behaviour-weighted Sinkhorn with an additive Euclidean cost, behaviour here is not a weight and not a suffix: it IS the local curvature of the distance, c_ik = c_l * exp(-a_ik). The transport column marginals are frozen to the Euclidean nearest-code counts, so curvature is structurally incapable of changing code usage; that is the property the previous mechanism lacked.
ideas.observables: (1) fraction of items whose level-l code differs from the geometry-off assignment, target 5-40%, with less than 1% meaning the curvature is inert; (2) exact equality of the per-level usage multiset with the Euclidean counts, logged every step; (3) exported support, which must be at least the same-run Euclidean support and is expected to stay at or above 247 level-1 codes / 7414 prefixes / 20223 three-token SIDs; (4) collision rate and L1 positive/negative hit rates should stay near the frozen baseline rather than 0.998 / 0.982 / 0.980; (5) successor prefix hit rate, the fraction of training transitions with code_l(u)=code_l(v), should rise above the geometry-off run; (6) Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 against the frozen 0.055537.
risks: The curvature carrier is only a 3-vector, so bandwidth is low; a_ik computed from Euclidean successor codes may be noisy early and behave like a random permutation; the Sinkhorn temperature derived from the measured cost gap can be unstable in early epochs; capacity matching limits codebook adaptation; cross-level SID collisions may rise even though per-level support is preserved; the curvature may act as a mild regulariser with less than 1% assignment change and no recall movement.
ideas.safeguards: psi maps into radius 0.95/sqrt(c_l) so sqrt(c_ik)*||.|| <= 0.95 < 1 always; the artanh argument is clamped to 1-1e-6; the Möbius denominator is clamped to 1e-12; Sinkhorn runs in the log domain for 10 iterations with largest-remainder repair of the column sums; tau is clamped; ties are broken deterministically; sigma_l is floored at 1e-6 and delta_l is set to 0 if the null is degenerate; c_l is clamped to [0.25, 4.0]; codes with u_k = 0 are excluded from the plan exactly as in the Euclidean pass; s_l falls back to the previous step's value if the batch is degenerate; the per-level usage-multiset equality is asserted and logged. Four-rank safety: the curvature profile is produced offline and read from a file by every rank; the Euclidean code table is recomputed identically on every rank from the replicated codebook after the DDP step; any gather is an equal-shape all_gather on all ranks; there is no rank-0-only broadcast or export inside the training loop.
ideas.spec_equations: for l in 1..3: s_l = max(quantile_0.9({||z_i^l||} U {||v_k||}), 1e-8); psi(x) = (0.95/sqrt(c_l)) * tanh(||x||/(2*s_l)) * x/max(||x||,1e-12); a_ik as above, detached; c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), detached; C_ik = d_{c_ik}(psi(z_i), psi(v_k)); u_k = #{i : argmin_k' ||z_i^l - v_k'|| = k}; tau = clamp(mean_i (C_i,(2) - C_i,(1)), 1e-3, 10); log-domain Sinkhorn for j=1..10, f_i = -tau*logsumexp_k(-C_ik/tau + g_k), g_k = -tau*logsumexp_i(-C_ik/tau + f_i) + tau*log(u_k/B); P from the normalised potentials; repair the column sums to u_k/B by largest remainder; c_ihat = argmax_k P_ik with ties by cost then code id; vbar_i = sum_k P_ik v_k; z_q = z_i + (v_{c_ihat} - z_i).detach() + (vbar_i - vbar_i.detach()); r_i^{l+1} = z_i^l - v_{c_ihat}. The loss is unchanged from the RQ-VAE baseline (reconstruction plus commitment); no new loss term and no new parameter.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are the per-level residual batch z_i^l (B x d), the codebook V_l (K x d), the top-20 training successor lists S(i), the detached Euclidean code table euc_l(.) over all training items, and the detached scalars (c_l, s_l, tau). Outputs are a code c_ihat in 1..K per item, the quantized vector z_q, the next residual r_i^{l+1}, and the plan P used for the straight-through gradient.

specification.text: Per level l, map the residual and the codes into a Poincaré ball with per-level curvature c_l (from the standardised behaviour-graph curvature profile), price each pair by C_ik = d_{c_ik}(psi(z_i), psi(v_k)) with c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), solve a Sinkhorn plan whose row sums are 1 and whose column sums are exactly the Euclidean nearest-code counts u_k of the same batch, take the code as argmax_k P_ik with a straight-through gradient through the soft code, and recurse on the residual. Column capacities equal to the Euclidean counts is the resolution guarantee: the per-level usage multiset, and therefore the exported support, is exactly the Euclidean one.

ideas.title: Capacity-frozen, successor-curvature-field Poincaré assignment for the RQ-VAE, with the code radius left untouched by construction

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: `kappa_hat[l,k] := 0` for all k, so `kappa_{l,k} = kappa_0` everywhere. The Poincare chart, the Sinkhorn plan, the uniform marginals and the code table are identical to the full run; only the per-code curvature differences disappear, so the plan becomes the curvature-uniform balanced transport plan. Isolates whether the behaviour field, rather than the balanced transport, carries the gain.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The run that is actually trained: per-code chart curvature from the training quotient graph, hard uniform column marginals, straight-through assignment, inherited code table, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, then the frozen Stage 3 protocol with no early stopping. One run, one seed; the switches exist in the code and are asserted correct in a unit test at B=8, K=4 against hand-computed Poincare distances, but no arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: `kappa_{l,k} := 0` for all k, so `dhat_k` is the ordinary Euclidean distance and the assignment is a Euclidean balanced transport with the same uniform marginals. The curvature measurement still runs and still produces `kappa_hat`, but `kappa_hat` now multiplies nothing that survives the `kappa -> 0` limit, so the behaviour signal is provably inert. Isolates the curved chart and, by construction, the coupling itself.
ideas.behavior_computation: Enumerated from TRAINING split interactions only, in order, giving a multiset `T_train` of directed pairs (u,v). For each level l each pair is mapped to `(A_l[u], A_l[v])` using the last-synced detached memberships, EMA-updated every 20 epochs from the current argmax assignment. Count, symmetrise (`W = N + N^T`), row-normalise, compute per-edge Ollivier curvature with an entropic W1 over the quotient graph, aggregate per node by W-weighted mean, standardise against a member-shuffle null (8 shuffles), clip to +-3 sigma. No gradient flows through any of it; it is a schedule producing 3 x 256 scalars every 20 epochs.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions (u -> v, v the next interaction in the same training sequence), aggregated into a code-level transition graph; the quantity the mechanism consumes is the Ollivier curvature of that quotient graph, i.e. how much the successor distributions of two codes overlap.
ideas.cost_estimate:
Frozen scale: 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, B = 1023 items per step, K = 256, L = 3, 3000 epochs.
  Per step: 3 levels x 1023 x 256 = 785,664 cost entries, each needing tanh/artanh/exp/log/sqrt; 8 Sinkhorn sweeps on the same matrices = ~6.3M elementwise ops plus ~30 small kernel launches; extra activations 3 x (1023x256) float32 = 3.1 MB. Estimated +3% to +6% step time, zero extra trainable parameters (the field is 3x256 scalars set by schedule, not by gradient).
  Curvature sync: 3000/20 = 150 syncs x 3 levels on a 65536-entry quotient graph with typically ~5e3 nonzero edges, each edge a 20-iteration Sinkhorn W1 over 256 bins: ~150 x 3 x 5e3 x 20 x 256 = 1.2e10 elementwise ops over the whole run, tens of seconds of GPU time; the 8 shuffle nulls multiply that by nine, still under a few minutes total.
  Collective cost: one `all_reduce(SUM)` of a fixed-shape float32 tensor [3,256,256] (768 kB) per sync, 150 times. Fixed shape, identical order on all four ranks, no variable-length transport support, no rank-0-only broadcast, no CPU tensor collective.
ideas.coupling_equation: `C_l[i,k] = dhat_{kappa_0 * exp(alpha * kappa_hat[l,k])}( rho_{...}(x_i^(l)), rho_{...}(c_{l,k}) )^2 / eps_l`, with `kappa_hat[l,k] = clip( (kappa_raw^{W_l}[l,k] - mu[k]) / (sigma[k]+1e-6), -3, 3 )` computed from the training transition counts `W_l`, and `P_l = argmin_{P in U(1/B, 1/K_l)} <P, C_l> - eps_l H(P)`.
ideas.coupling_path: Single path: training transitions -> code quotient graph -> standardised Ollivier curvature `kappa_hat[l,k]` -> per-code chart curvature `kappa_{l,k}` -> Poincare chart distance in the cost matrix `C_l` -> Sinkhorn plan `P_l` with uniform marginals -> forward SID token `a_i^(l)`. The behaviour term is multiplied into the curvature, the curvature is the only thing that changes the metric, and the metric is the only thing that changes the plan; drop behaviour (`kappa_hat = 0`) and every code shares one curvature so the plan becomes the curvature-uniform one; drop geometry (`kappa = 0`) and the metric is Euclidean so the behaviour field has no channel. Neither acts alone.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The profile can be expressed as a per-code chart that only reorders items, while a hard equipartition supplies the resolution the previous round lost. Confirmed in the single run by: (i) used codes `U_l >= 0.9*K_l` after the first sync instead of 2/256; (ii) exported SID counts at least 247/7414/20223 and collision rate far below 0.998; (iii) the level-1 positive-minus-negative hit-rate gap growing past 0.02 (baseline gap 0.002), i.e. the first token starts carrying information; (iv) Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.055537, reaching 0.065 if the resolution gain translates. If (i)-(iii) hold and (iv) does not, the diagnosis is that the coarse partition was forced too flat and the chart field is not the limiter.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantisation, in the assignment step of every level: it defines the cost matrix that the entropic transport plan minimises, hence which code each item inherits at each level. It does not touch the code parameters, their norms, the codebook sizes, the loss weights, the decoder or the generative recommender.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance with schedule-set per-code curvature `kappa_{l,k} = kappa_0 * exp(alpha * kappa_hat_{l,k})`, where `kappa_0 = 1/s_l^2` comes from the measured residual RMS and `kappa_hat` is the clipped standardised behaviour curvature. The distance is normalised by the conformal factor at the code, `dhat_k = d_k / lambda_k(c)`, so the chart reduces exactly to the Euclidean metric as `kappa -> 0`.
ideas.key_change: Each RQ level solves its assignment as a Sinkhorn transport problem whose per-code cost uses a Poincare distance in the code's own curvature chart `kappa_{l,k}`, with uniform column marginals; the per-code curvatures come from the standardised Ollivier curvature of the K-node code-transition quotient graph built from training transitions under the previous sync's memberships, so curvature can only permute items between codes, never remove codes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition set is built exclusively from training-split sequences. Validation and test sequences are never enumerated, never mapped to codes, never enter the quotient graph or the null. The null shuffles only training memberships, so `sigma` is a property of the training split's own size and degree distribution. The 4096-item probe used by the alpha safeguard is drawn from training items only. The exported SID is a deterministic function of the training-only code table, training-only transition graph and training memberships, and since the protocol has no early stopping there is no validation signal that could select an epoch. Nothing in the assignment consumes a validation or test interaction.
ideas.motivation: The previous round proved that the standardised behaviour-graph curvature profile carries real signal (Spearman -0.20 over 115 mechanism families on the level-1 minus level-3 deviation) but that spending it on the per-level code radius destroys the thing recall actually needs: resolution. That run exported 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, level-1 positive/negative hit rates 0.982/0.980 (the first token carried no information), and scored 0.041888. The underlying pathology is level collapse in the first RQ level: 2 of 256 codes alive. This idea gives the curvature a place to act where it cannot shrink anything, and separately removes the collapse by construction.
ideas.novelty: Three things absent from CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ, BRad-RQ, CURVCTRL-SID, behcone-prefix-rq, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, succboost-geoshift, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ and BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ. (1) Curvature is a FIELD, one value per code per level, `kappa_{l,k} = kappa_0 * exp(alpha * kappa_hat_{l,k})`; all earlier mechanisms set one number per level and applied it to the whole level. (2) Curvature acts on the DISTANCE CHART of each code, never on the code vector, its norm, its count or the space's radius; the code table keeps the inherited parameterisation bit for bit. (3) The assignment is an entropic optimal transport problem with hard uniform column marginals, so code utilisation is fixed at B/K by the constraint, not by a loss weight; the resolution guarantee is a constraint, not a hyperparameter. Curvature reorders who goes where and is structurally forbidden from changing how many codes are used.
ideas.observables: Used codes per level `U_l` (2/13/56 in the failed arm; 247/7414/20223 distinct SIDs in the frozen baseline); distinct SID count and collision rate; level-1 and level-2 positive-minus-negative hit-rate gap (baseline 0.982 vs 0.980); prefix-conditional entropy `H(next prefix | current prefix)` per level measured on the training split only; Spearman correlation between `kappa_hat` and the level's realised utilisation; variation of information between the current assignment and the previous sync's assignment (small but nonzero, showing the field is doing something stable); Stage3 test_recall@10.
risks: Hard uniform marginals may be too rigid for a genuinely hierarchical corpus, splitting natural coarse clusters and inflating prefix entropy; utilisation would be perfect while level-1 accuracy degrades. The one-epoch-lag feedback (curvature from last memberships, memberships from curvature) may oscillate or lock into a self-confirming partition; the 20-epoch sync and the alpha decay are the only damping. On a 65536-entry quotient graph many codes have few edges, so `kappa_raw` can be noise-dominated even after shuffle standardisation, and the +-3 sigma clip may then produce a nearly uniform field that degenerates to the geometry-only behaviour. Ollivier W1 on a sparse quotient graph is a crude proxy and may be uncorrelated with the item-level curvature measured in round 1. Forcing exactly 4 items per code per step means level 1 can no longer represent a dominant generic prefix, which may be right for the export and wrong for the training signal.
ideas.safeguards:
Distances: clamp the Mobius sum norm to `1 - 1e-6` before artanh; clamp the ball radius to `0.9/sqrt(kappa)` when embedding; add `1e-8` inside every sqrt, log and division; clamp `||z|| >= 1e-8` before the `rho` division so `rho_k(0)=0` is exact.
  Curvature: clamp `kappa` to `[1e-3*kappa_0, 1e3*kappa_0]` so the chart can never invert or vanish; clamp `kappa_hat` to +-3 sigma so one noisy code cannot dominate; add `1e-6` to `sigma`.
  Transport: subtract the row-minimum of `C` before `exp`; if a row has all-equal `C` under float precision, fall back to the uniform plan for that row; if `B < K_l` so a uniform column marginal is unattainable, restrict that step to a fixed cycling subset of `K_l` codes of size B chosen by a fixed permutation, so all codes are covered across steps.
  Utilisation: the automatic alpha halving when a level's training-probe utilisation drops below `0.9*K_l`; it only ever shrinks the curvature spread, never the codebook, and is capped at 5 halvings.
  Determinism and deadlock: the code-transition counts live in a fixed `[L,K,K]` float32 buffer, zeroed first and filled by `index_add`, then `all_reduce(SUM)` with every rank participating in the same order and the same shape; no rank-0-only path, no CPU-side broadcast, no variable-length transport support. Export writes the SID CSV from rank 0 after a barrier and every other rank proceeds to the next epoch without waiting on a broadcast; the shuffle null uses a seed derived only from the level and the sync index, so all four ranks generate the same shuffle without communication.
  Feedback stability: the field is refreshed from a detached EMA of memberships (momentum 0.9), never from the current step, so the assignment and the field cannot chase each other within an epoch.
ideas.spec_equations:
```
# per step, per level l
s_l        = 0.99*s_l + 0.01*RMS(||x^(l)||);   kappa_0 = 1/(s_l^2 + 1e-8)
kappa[l,k] = kappa_0 * exp(alpha * kappa_hat[l,k])      # behaviour-off: kappa_hat:=0 ; geometry-off: kappa:=0
y_i        = rho_{kappa[l,k]}(x_i)                       # broadcast over k
ct_k       = rho_{kappa[l,k]}(c_{l,k})
D2[i,k]    = d_{kappa[l,k]}(y_i, ct_k)^2 / (lambda_{kappa[l,k]}(ct_k)^2 + 1e-8)
C[i,k]     = D2[i,k] / (median(D2) + 1e-8)
Kmat       = exp(-(C - rowmin(C)))
for t in 1..8:
    Kmat = Kmat / (rowsum(Kmat) * B)          # row marginal 1/B
    Kmat = Kmat / (colsum(Kmat) * K_l)        # col marginal 1/K_l
P      = Kmat / rowsum(Kmat)
a_i    = argmax_k P[i,k]
loss   = recon(x_i - sum_k P[i,k] c_{l,k}  [straight-through])
       + lambda_commit * || x_i - sg(sum_k P[i,k] c_{l,k}) ||^2      # inherited loss, unchanged

# every 20 epochs, all four ranks, no gradient
N[k,k']      = bincount(A[u]*K + A[v] for (u,v) in T_train).reshape(K,K);  W = N + N.T
Prow         = N / clamp(rowsum(N), 1)
kap(k,k')    = 1 - sinkhorn_W1(Prow[k], Prow[k'], d_Gamma, iters=20) / d_Gamma(k,k')
kappa_raw[k] = sum_k' W[k,k']*kap(k,k') / clamp(sum_k' W[k,k'], 1)
mu, sigma    = mean and std over 8 member-shuffles of kappa_raw
kappa_hat    = clamp((kappa_raw - mu)/(sigma + 1e-6), -3, 3)
if used_codes_on_train_probe(level l) < 0.9*K_l:  alpha *= 0.5
```
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs:
Input (per step): `x_i^(l)` for i=1..B (encoder output or residual), the code table `c_{l,k}` for k=1..K_l, the current field `kappa_hat[l,·]` (a 256-vector refreshed on schedule), the measured scale `s_l`.
  Output (per step): a hard token `a_i^(l)` in {1..K_l} per item per level, the soft plan `P_l` used for the straight-through gradient, and the next residual `x_i^(l+1) = x_i^(l) - c_{l,a_i^(l)}`.
  Input (per sync): the training transition pair list, the last-synced memberships `A_l` over all training items, one fixed shuffle seed and shuffle count 8.
  Output (per sync): the `3 x 256` curvature field plus recorded diagnostics (`kappa_raw`, `mu`, `sigma`, utilisation, conditional prefix entropy, collision rate). The field is broadcast inside the same fixed-shape all_reduce, so every rank holds an identical copy with no separate communication.

specification.text:
Notation: level l in {1,2,3}, K_l codes per level, batch B items (B = 1023 at the frozen scale).
  Code table: `c_{l,k} in R^d`, inherited parameterisation, inherited init, inherited K_l. Untouched by this mechanism.
  Residual: `x_i^(1) = E(u_i)`; `x_i^(l+1) = x_i^(l) - c_{l, a_i^(l)}`.
  Scale: `s_l = 0.99*s_l + 0.01*RMS(||x_i^(l)||)`. Curvature base `kappa_0 = 1/(s_l^2 + 1e-8)` (derived from the measured residual scale, no free constant).
  Ball embedding: `rho_k(z) = (tanh(sqrt(k)||z||/2) / (sqrt(k)||z||)) * z`, `rho_k(0)=0`.
  Poincare distance: `d_k(x,y) = (2/sqrt(k)) * artanh( sqrt(k) * || (-x)(+)y || )`, with `(-x)(+)y = ((1-k|x|^2)y - (1-k|y|^2)x) / (1 - 2k<x,y> + k^2|x|^2|y|^2)`.
  Local chart distance (the object the mechanism spends): `dhat_k(x,y) = d_k(x,y) / lambda_k(y)`, `lambda_k(y) = 2/(1 - k|y|^2)`. Note `dhat_k -> ||x-y||` as `k -> 0`.
  Assignment cost: `C_l[i,k] = dhat_{kappa_{l,k}}( rho_{kappa_{l,k}}(x_i^(l)), rho_{kappa_{l,k}}(c_{l,k}) )^2 / eps_l`, `eps_l = median(C_l)` detached.
  Transport: `P_l = Sinkhorn(C_l, r = 1/B, c = 1/K_l, iters = 8)` on kernel `exp(-C_l)`.
  Forward assignment `a_i^(l) = argmax_k P_l[i,k]`; straight-through: code term uses `sum_k P_l[i,k] c_{l,k}` with argmax as the forward value and the soft plan as the backward gradient.
  Curvature field (schedule, no gradient), synced every S = 20 epochs from last-synced detached memberships `A_l[i]`:
    `N_l[k,k'] = #{ (u,v) in T_train : A_l[u]=k, A_l[v]=k' }`, `W_l = N_l + N_l^T`.
    `P_l = N_l / max(rowsum, 1)`.
    For each edge `(k,k')` with `W_l[k,k']>0`: `kappa(k,k') = 1 - W1(P_l[k,·], P_l[k',·]) / d_Gamma(k,k')`, `d_Gamma` = hop distance on the quotient graph, W1 = entropic Wasserstein with the same Sinkhorn solver (20 iterations).
    `kappa_raw[l,k] = sum_{k'} W_l[k,k'] kappa(k,k') / sum_{k'} W_l[k,k']`.
    Null: shuffle item->code labels `A_l` uniformly (fixed torch seed), recompute `kappa_raw` 8 times (documented default) giving `mu[k], sigma[k]`.
    `kappa_hat[l,k] = clip( (kappa_raw[l,k] - mu[k]) / (sigma[k]+1e-6), -3, +3 )`.
    `kappa_{l,k} = kappa_0 * exp(alpha * kappa_hat[l,k])`, `alpha_0 = 1`.
  Safeguard schedule: after each sync, on a fixed 4096-item TRAINING probe compute `U_l` (codes used) and `D` (distinct SIDs); if `U_l < 0.9*K_l` then `alpha <- 0.5*alpha` (automatic decay, capped at 5 halvings). No searching.
  Switches (present in code, all correct, none trained as an arm): BEHAVIOUR off sets `kappa_hat := 0` so all codes share curvature `kappa_0`; GEOMETRY off sets `kappa_{l,k} := 0` so `dhat` is Euclidean and `kappa_hat` has no channel; BOTH ON is the full path above.

ideas.title: Per-code chart curvature on the training behaviour quotient graph, spent as a hard-marginal entropic transport assignment that cannot give up codebook resolution.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAVIOUR_OFF=1 sets s_e = 0 for all codes and all levels (kappa is still measured and logged), so every gain is 1 and the assignment reduces provably to the Euclidean argmin; this is the correct switch and it must compile and train, but this round runs no arm with it set.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAVIOUR_OFF=0 and GEOMETRY_OFF=0, the only configuration trained this round: the full per-code chart field from the null-standardised training-graph curvature inside the artanh assignment score, with the guard band active.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOMETRY_OFF=1 replaces q_e by the Euclidean ratio ||r - e||/rho_l in the softmax while s_e is still computed and written to the log, so the curvature field is present but the curved operator is absent; no arm is trained with it set.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAINING split only: for each training user sequence, consecutive (i_t, i_t+1) pairs increment n_ij; the item graph has the 24556 training items as nodes and the observed directed pairs as edges; the lazy random-walk measure m_i = 0.5 delta_i + 0.5 p_i is compared to m_j by entropic Wasserstein-1 with eps = 1/(2 max_out_degree), and kappa_OR(i,j) = 1 - W1/dist(i,j). Item curvature kappa_i is the out-edge mean; code curvature is the mean over the code's assigned items, taken from the previous epoch's assignments, standardised against R = 8 size-preserving member shuffles and clipped to +-3. Nothing in this path is differentiable and nothing in it is updated by backpropagation.
ideas.behavior_signal: The standardised, code-local mean Ollivier-Ricci curvature s_e of the directed training item-transition graph restricted to the items each codeword served in the previous epoch; equivalently a per-code measure of how tree-like (branching, negative curvature) versus clique-like (redundant, positive curvature) the successor structure of that code's cell is.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time offline pass: 24556 nodes, ~1e6 directed edges, Sinkhorn W1 per edge on CPU, roughly 5-15 minutes wall clock, executed independently on every rank (or read from an identical precomputed file on every rank) so there is no rank-0 broadcast. Per-step cost at the frozen scale: 3 levels x (batch x 256) artanh plus a clip and a min/max, i.e. about 786k artanh evaluations per step at batch 1024, roughly 0.2-0.5 ms of GPU time, under 2% of step wall clock over 24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps (<25 s total). Per-epoch statistics: one all_reduce of 3x256 floats plus 8 shuffles over 24556 items, about 1 ms per epoch, 3000 epochs -> a few seconds. Memory: one 256-float vector per level, plus a 24556-float curvature vector.
ideas.coupling_equation: q_e(r) = artanh( clip( tanh(1) * exp(-s_e/2) * ||r - e|| / rho_l , 0 , 1-1e-6 ) ), with s_e = clip( ( mean_{i in A_e} kappa_OR(i) - mu_null ) / sigma_null , -3, +3 ) and the guard q_e <- clip( q_e , 0.5 q_e^0 , 2 q_e^0 ), q_e^0 = artanh(tanh(1)||r-e||/rho_l); the behaviour term is exp(-s_e/2), the curved term is artanh.
ideas.coupling_path: kappa_OR (training graph) -> per-code mean over the previous epoch's cell A_e -> null-standardised s_e (gradient-free) -> gain g_e = exp(-s_e/2) -> curvature c_e = c0_l g_e^2 -> Poincare distance q_e = artanh(sqrt(c_e)||r-e||) -> guard-banded assignment score -> argmin/softmax -> SID tokens. Removing the behaviour term sets s_e = 0 and therefore g_e = 1 for every code, which makes q_e = artanh(tanh(1)||r-e||/rho_l) a single common strictly increasing map of ||r-e||, so the argmin collapses exactly onto the baseline Euclidean assignment; removing the geometry replaces artanh(...) by the identity on ||r-e||/rho_l, so c_e is computed but no longer enters any computation. Both removals change the core computation, and neither touches a radius.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The mechanism is worth keeping if the code-local curvature field is anti-correlated with successor predictability in the way the graph suggests: codes sitting in tree-like (negative Ollivier) transition regions are exactly the codes whose current Euclidean cells mix several incompatible successor distributions, and giving them a slightly more permissive (concave, larger effective radius at fixed boundary) chart while tightening clique-like codes raises per-code successor purity, which raises next-token predictability of the SID prefix, which Stage 3 converts into Recall@10 above 0.065. Observation: the fraction of items whose argmin changes versus the neutral chart should be non-trivial (expected a few percent), per-code successor entropy should fall on the codes with large |s_e|, the level cardinalities should stay within 0.9-1.1x of 247/7414/20223, and the L1 hit rate should move away from the uninformative 0.982/0.980 of the failed round. If instead fewer than 0.5% of assignments change, the guard band has made the mechanism a no-op and the hypothesis is disconfirmed by the single run itself.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE's assignment step at every level, in the distance that scores residual r against codeword e before the softmax and before the commitment / reconstruction losses; it never enters the codeword update, the codebook radius, the commitment weight, the encoder, or the decoder.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: The Poincare ball distance from the chart origin to the residual, d_P(0,u) = 2 artanh(sqrt(c) ||u||) with trainable-but-frozen negative curvature magnitude c = c_e per codeword, emitted as the dimensionless score q_e = artanh(sqrt(c_e)||r-e||); the per-code curvature is anchored at c0_l = tanh(1)^2/rho_l^2 so that a residual of the measured scale rho_l maps to exactly 1.0 in the neutral chart.
ideas.key_change: Each RQ level's assignment score replaces the Euclidean residual norm by a per-codeword Poincare chart distance q_e(r) = artanh(g_e * tanh(1) * ||r-e|| / rho_l), where g_e = exp(-s_e/2) and s_e is the null-standardised mean training-graph Ollivier-Ricci curvature of the items that codeword e covered in the previous epoch; each q_e is then clipped to a [0.5, 2] band around its neutral (g_e = 1) value. Codewords, their radii, their number and their EMA update stay exactly as in the inherited baseline.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The graph, the measures and kappa_i are built exclusively from training-split sequences; the validation and test interactions are never read, never touched during encoding, and never used to fit the transition graph or the per-code means. The standardisation null is a member shuffle of TRAINING items among codes, so it carries no split information either. rho_l is measured from the run's own epoch-0 residuals on training batches. Because the field enters only as a frozen schedule with no gradient, no validation or test signal can propagate into the SID construction, and the per-code means are recomputed from training assignments only.
ideas.motivation: The previous round proved that the standardised training-graph curvature profile does track which SID tables turn out well (Spearman -0.20 over 115 families) but that spending it on the per-level code radius destroys the codebook: kappa_hat [0.00,-8.96,-25.55] -> delta [0.702,0.298,-1.000] -> radius [0.0381,0.0312,0.0163] gave 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, L1 hit rates 0.982/0.980 and Stage3 test_recall@10 0.041888 against the inherited 0.0446 and the frozen baseline 0.055537 (247/7414/20223). The problem this idea addresses is therefore not "how do we use curvature" but "how do we let curvature reshape which items a codeword accepts, while the codebook keeps every bit of the resolution it had". The mechanism gives every codeword its own local curvature chart, derived from the behaviour of the items that codeword actually serves, and admits residuals through that chart's metric; the codeword vectors, their norms, their count, and their update rule are copied byte-identically from the inherited baseline.
ideas.novelty: Different from CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ (which spent curvature on c_l and rho_l, i.e. on the space's radius), from BRad-RQ (which moved items radially using behaviour-ranking), from CURVCTRL-SID (which spent a prefix-transition score on a level learning rate), from poincare-frechet-successor-codebook (curved codebook updates), from LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ / behcone-prefix-rq (conical prefix constraints) and from the Euclidean RQ it inherits. Here curvature is a CODE-LOCAL field living only inside the assignment score, the level-global profile is deliberately made inert (a level-uniform gain cancels in the argmin, which is why round 1 could only express it by moving the radius), and the effect on the partition is bounded by a derived guard band so that the mechanism is provably a bounded perturbation of the baseline Voronoi diagram rather than a rescaling of it. Resolution is protected structurally, not empirically: nothing that determines code scale, code count or code lifetime is a function of curvature.
ideas.observables: (a) SID assignment: fraction of items whose hard argmin changes versus the neutral chart, per-level code cardinality, and the deviation of those cardinalities from 247/7414/20223 (must stay inside 0.9-1.1x, this is the resolution certificate); (b) gradient/parameter update: the per-code assignment mass and the codeword EMA trajectories, which must shift only through the changed assignment counts, never through a curvature term in the loss; (c) prefix behaviour predictability: per-code successor-distribution entropy, the level-1 positive/negative hit rates (must move off 0.982/0.980), and the training-split bigram log-likelihood of the SID prefixes; (d) Stage3 test_recall@10, the only judgement, target above 0.065 and in no case below the frozen baseline 0.055537.
risks: s_e is noisy for small cells even after standardisation, so the field may be dominated by high-count codes and act as a near-constant; artanh saturation can make a code reject everything beyond a short radius, which the guard band contains but which can still waste that code's capacity; the lagged EMA creates a feedback loop (assignment -> s_e -> assignment) that may oscillate, mitigated only by the per-epoch update rate and the clip; a 2x bounded gain may simply be too weak to matter at the partition level; and even a cleaner partition may not convert into recall if the Stage 3 transformer already memorises prefix idiosyncrasies. The mechanism also inherits any bias in the transition graph towards popular items.
ideas.safeguards: (1) artanh argument clamped to [0, 1-1e-6]; artanh(1-1e-6) ~ 7.25 so no infinity. (2) Empty or tiny codes keep s_e = 0 and their c_e = c0_l, so the field cannot kill a code. (3) The [0.5, 2] guard band bounds every code's effective accepting radius, so no codeword can gain or lose more than a factor two of reach; this is the resolution certificate and is checked every epoch against 0.9-1.1x of 247/7414/20223. (4) sqrt inside sqrt(c_e) is floored at 1e-12 because c_e > 0 by construction; rho_l floored at 1e-6. (5) Curvature is computed under no_grad from a frozen tensor, so it cannot receive or emit gradients. (6) Any per-code statistic that needs more than one rank uses all_reduce with every rank calling it, at epoch boundaries only; the curvature tensor is either recomputed identically on each rank or read from the same file on each rank, never broadcast from rank 0, and the SID export is written independently by each rank to its own shard. (7) A dead-code reset from the baseline is retained unchanged and is curvature-independent. (8) NaN guard: if any q is non-finite the step falls back to q0 for that level and logs a counter.
ideas.spec_equations:
K = ollivier(training_transition_graph)                         # frozen, no_grad
for epoch in 1..3000:
    s_raw[e] = mean_{i in A_e^{epoch-1}} K[i]                                # per level, A_e from last epoch
    mu, sd   = null_stats(s_raw, R=8, preserve=|A_e|)                        # member shuffle
    s[e]     = clip((s_raw[e]-mu)/sd, -3, 3)
    g[e]     = exp(-s[e]/2)
    c[e]     = tanh(1)^2 / rho_l^2 * g[e]^2
    for step in 1..24:                                                        # per batch, per level
        d2   = ||r - e||^2                                                    # B x 256
        x    = sqrt(c[e]) * sqrt(d2)
        q0   = artanh(clip(tanh(1)*sqrt(d2)/rho_l, 0, 1-1e-6))
        q    = artanh(clip(x, 0, 1-1e-6))
        q    = clip(q, 0.5*q0, 2*q0)
        p    = softmax(-q / tau_baseline, dim=codes)
        k    = argmin_e q                                                      # SID token
    codeword update, commitment loss, reconstruction loss unchanged from baseline
rho_l = all_reduce_sum(||r-e||^2) / all_reduce_sum(count) at end of epoch 0, then frozen.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the residual matrix r (B x D) of a level, the codeword matrix E (K x D) unchanged from the baseline, the frozen per-item curvature vector K (24556), the previous epoch's assignment counts, rho_l (3 floats), tau_baseline. Outputs: the per-code curvature vector c_e (K), the guarded score matrix q (B x K), the soft assignment p (B x K) used by the existing losses, and the hard code index k that becomes the SID token; plus the logged s_e and the cardinality certificate.

specification.text: (1) Offline, training split only, gradient-free: build the directed item transition graph from consecutive in-session pairs of the training sequences, counts n_ij; node measure m_i = 0.5*delta_i + 0.5*p_i with p_i(j) = n_ij / sum_j n_ij; kappa_OR(i,j) = 1 - W1(m_i, m_j)/dist(i,j) with W1 by Sinkhorn (entropic eps = 1/(2*max_out_degree), 50 iterations), dist the unweighted graph hop distance; kappa_i = mean over out-edges of i. Store as a frozen 24556-vector K. (2) At the end of every epoch (with the previous epoch's hard assignments A_e per level), compute s_e_raw = mean_{i in A_e} K_i and s_e = clip( (s_e_raw - mu_null)/sigma_null, -3, +3 ) where mu_null/sigma_null come from R=8 member shuffles that permute items among codewords preserving each |A_e| exactly (empty codes excluded, they keep s_e = 0). (3) rho_l = RMS of ||r - e|| over the level's residuals at the end of epoch 0, all_reduced over ranks, frozen thereafter. c0_l = tanh(1)^2 / rho_l^2, c_e = c0_l * exp(-s_e). (4) Per step: x = sqrt(c_e)*||r-e||, q_e = artanh(min(x, 1-1e-6)), q_e^0 = artanh(min(tanh(1)*||r-e||/rho_l, 1-1e-6)), q_e <- clip(q_e, 0.5*q_e^0, 2*q_e^0); softmax over -q_e/tau with the baseline's tau unchanged.

ideas.title: Per-codeword Poincare chart curvature, spent on the assignment metric with the codebook radius left untouched

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The flag sets z_l = 0 for l=1,2,3, hence b_l = 0 and kappa_l = k_ref,l for all levels; the Mobius geometry is still switched on and the code radius/count are unchanged. This run has the same code scale and the same operator but no behaviour profile, so any difference is attributable to the behaviour term.
ideas.ablation_both_on: kappa_l is the real coarse-referenced, null-standardised profile and the Mobius residual operator is active at levels 2 and 3. This is the single trained candidate; the two switches above exist in the code but are not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The flag sets kappa_l = 0 exactly for all levels, so exp_0 is the identity and (+) is ordinary addition; bend returns r - c and the model is exactly the Euclidean RQ-VAE on the same codebooks. The behaviour profile is still computed and logged but has no effect. This run isolates the curved operation.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, over all training sequences, count directed pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) with immediate repeats suppressed, giving a sparse item transition matrix W (24556 x 24556). At recompute time, take the current DDP-synchronised encoder and codebooks, encode the 24556 training items once, assign prefixes 1..l-1, and sum W over prefix pairs to build the sparse quotient graph A_l (level 1 is the item graph itself). Compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature per edge (lazy random walk with standard 0.5 laziness, Wasserstein-1 via a sparse min-cost solve or Sinkhorn with a fixed small epsilon), and take the transition-count-weighted mean as kappa_raw,l. Null: B=10 replicates; for level 1 rewire W by degree-preserving stub matching; for levels 2,3 permute the item-to-prefix labels while preserving each prefix size, then recompute. z_l is the standardised deviation. Everything is computed with torch.no_grad and stored as a schedule tensor; it never enters the backward graph.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions and user-interest branching extracted from training sequences, aggregated at each RQ level into a prefix-level quotient graph whose standardised Ollivier-Ricci curvature profile is the behaviour term.
ideas.cost_estimate: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps, batch ~1023): the bend adds per item per bent level two exp_0 (d tanh), one Mobius add (~12d mul/add) and two norms, about 40d flops; with d=64 and two bent levels this is ~5 MFLOP per step, under 0.5 ms on one GPU, about 0.2-0.5 percent of step time, ~30-40 s over the whole run. The curvature schedule runs 30 times: one full encode of 24556 items (24 batches), prefix aggregation, edge curvature and 10 null shuffles, roughly 1-3 min on one CPU core per recompute (30-90 min total, 1-3 percent of a multi-hour four-rank run). No new trainable parameters, no extra forward pass in the training step, no collective.
ideas.coupling_equation: r_l^{in} = ||r_{l-1} - c_{l-1}|| * ( (-exp_0^{kappa_l}(c_{l-1})) (+)_{kappa_l} exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_{l-1}) ) / || (-exp_0^{kappa_l}(c_{l-1})) (+)_{kappa_l} exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_{l-1}) ||, with kappa_l = clip( k_ref,l * exp( (z_1 - z_l)/2 ), 0.22*k_ref,l, 4.48*k_ref,l ), z_l = clip( (kappa_raw,l - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, -3, +3 ), and k_ref,l = 1/m_l^2 measured from the training residual scale. The behaviour term is (z_1 - z_l); the curved term is exp_0^{kappa_l} and (+)_{kappa_l}; the Euclidean limit is kappa_l = 0.
ideas.coupling_path: Training behaviour graph -> quotient graph at each RQ level -> null-standardised Ollivier curvature z_l -> coarse-referenced bend b_l = z_1 - z_l -> level curvature kappa_l -> Mobius exp/add in bend_kappa -> direction of r_l entering level l -> level-l nearest-code assignment -> prefix and SID tokens -> Stage3. Removing behaviour (z_l = 0) flattens kappa_l to k_ref,l and changes the direction of r_2 and r_3. Removing geometry (kappa_l = 0) makes exp_0 the identity and (+) ordinary addition, so r_l = r_{l-1} - c_{l-1} and the path is Euclidean RQ. Either switch changes the same tensor path and therefore the assignment.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the coarse-to-fine curvature deviation is spent on the residual direction instead of the code radius, then fine-level code boundaries align with behaviour sub-communities while the codebook keeps the baseline resolution; the Stage3 model then sees finer tokens that are predictable from the coarse prefix, and test_recall@10 rises above the inherited 0.0446 and the frozen 0.055537 toward 0.065. It is worth keeping only if the counterfactual assignment sensitivity is non-trivial (a measurable fraction of items changes level-2/3 code when b_l is zeroed or kappa_l is set to 0) AND the exported table still has at least the inherited 247/7414/20223 distinct L1/L2/L3 counts with a collision rate near the baseline rather than 0.998.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the RQ quantization path between levels: the curved operator transforms the residual that enters levels 2 and 3, before the level's nearest-code search. It does not act on the code radius rho_l, the code count K_l, the assignment metric, the commitment weight, the encoder, or the decoder.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature -kappa_l (kappa_l > 0), with Mobius addition, exponential map at the origin exp_0^k(v) = tanh(sqrt(k)||v||) v/(sqrt(k)||v||), logarithm log_0^k, and the geodesic direction of the residual taken at the chosen code, w = (-q) (+) p. kappa_l is fixed per level and per 100-epoch block (not backpropagated); it is bounded to [0.22, 4.48] * k_ref,l by the z clip.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean RQ residual r_{l+1} = r_l - c_l with a unit hyperbolic direction times the original Euclidean residual norm, r_{l+1} = ||r_l - c_l|| * unit( (-exp(c_l)) (+) exp(r_l) ) in a Poincare ball whose curvature kappa_l is a detached, null-standardised, coarse-referenced behaviour profile, applied to the residual entering levels 2 and 3 (level 1 stays Euclidean). Nothing else changes: same encoder, same codebook sizes, same code-radius rule, same losses, same Stage3 protocol.
ideas.leakage_boundary: W is built exclusively from training-split sequences; validation and test sequences are never read, and no validation or test item is added to the graph or to the prefix map used for curvature. The null shuffles permute only training items. The schedule uses only the training item universe and the current codebook, which itself is trained on the training split. The exported SID table is built from the training item universe only. No validation or test interaction, reward, or click can enter kappa_l or the residual operator, and the Stage3 protocol remains frozen and untouched.
ideas.motivation: Round 20261102_031529_470 spent the null-standardised behaviour-graph curvature on the code radius rho_l inside the RQ-VAE assignment and collapsed the codebook (2 first-level codes, 13 prefixes, 56 SIDs, collision 0.998, L1 positive/negative hit rates 0.982/0.980, Stage3 test_recall@10 0.041888). The recommendation problem is still the one the correlation analysis identified: the coarse level should stay flat and the fine levels should be more curved, so that items inside one coarse prefix split into behaviourally meaningful sub-branches, which is what the generative model needs to predict fine SID tokens. This proposal obtains that profile without touching any code scale.
ideas.novelty: In every earlier mechanism the curvature changes the codebook (radius, assignment metric, codebook update, or a code-level loss). Here the curvature changes only the DIRECTION of the inter-level residual, and the residual norm is preserved exactly, so the code vectors, their count, their radius and the commitment weight are unchanged in form from the frozen baseline. The curvature magnitude is expressed in units of the measured median residual norm of that level, so the bend is scale-free; the profile is the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the level's own behaviour quotient graph, referenced to the coarse level (z_1 - z_l), which is exactly the quantity the earlier 115-family analysis found predictive (Spearman -0.20 for the level-1 minus level-3 deviation). No prior mechanism bends the residual direction.
ideas.observables: (1) Exported table resolution: distinct L1 codes, L2 prefixes, L3 SIDs, and collision rate, compared with the frozen 247/7414/20223 and with the failed 2/13/56 and 0.998. (2) Per-level code-usage entropy, compared with its own epoch-0 value. (3) L1 positive and negative hit rates, which must not both sit at ~0.98. (4) Counterfactual assignment sensitivity measured forward-only inside the single run: the fraction of training items whose level-2 and level-3 code changes when b_l is set to 0 (behaviour-off counterfactual) and when kappa_l is set to 0 (Euclidean counterfactual); this proves the coupling acts without training a second arm. (5) The measured kappa_l and b_l profiles and the distribution of realised bend angles. (6) Stage3 test_recall@10, target above 0.065, with 0.055537 as the frozen reference.
risks: The direction bend could be too weak in high dimension (residuals are nearly orthogonal to codes) and act as noise; the level-2 and level-3 quotient curvatures are estimated on thousands of small prefixes and may be unstable despite null standardisation; the codebook/quotient feedback loop could oscillate (mitigated by the 100-epoch schedule, the z clip and the usage monitor); the generative Stage3 model consumes only tokens, so a geometrically nicer residual may not translate into prefix predictability; Mobius arithmetic near the ball boundary can lose precision in float32.
ideas.safeguards: (1) Exact norm preservation: the output is nv * unit(w), so no level can shrink or grow the residual scale; this is the direct answer to the CURVALLOC failure. (2) The code radius rho_l, code count K_l, commitment weight and assignment metric are never functions of kappa_l; the codebook remains the baseline RQ-VAE codebook. (3) Ball safety: ||exp_0^k(v)|| < 1/sqrt(k) for every finite v; clamp ||p|| and ||q|| to 0.999/sqrt(k) and clamp the Mobius denominator to at least 1e-6. (4) Float32 bend with float64 graph curvature; if any r_{l+1} is NaN or Inf, fall back to the Euclidean v for that batch and level and increment a counter. (5) Curvature is clipped to z in [-3,3] and kappa to [0.22, 4.48] k_ref, both derived from the clip, not tuned. (6) Usage monitor at every recompute: if a level's usage entropy falls below 0.9 times its epoch-0 value, set b_l = 0 for the next block (documented default, measured reference). (7) No collective in the training loop: the transition matrix and the null permutations are built once before training and saved; every rank loads the same file and recomputes the quotient curvature locally from the DDP-synchronised codebook, so there is no rank-0 broadcast, no oversized transport and no rank-0 export deadlock. (8) The schedule runs at epoch boundaries in eval mode with torch.no_grad; it is a schedule/penalty-like quantity, never a backpropagated one.
ideas.spec_equations:
Mobius: x (+) y = ((1 + 2k<x,y> + k||y||^2)x + (1 - k||x||^2)y) / (1 + 2k<x,y> + k^2||x||^2||y||^2). Exp: exp_0^k(v) = tanh(sqrt(k)||v||) * v/(sqrt(k)||v||), exp_0^k(0)=0. Bend pseudocode:
  v = r - c; nv = ||v||
  if nv < 1e-8: return zeros_like(r)
  p = exp_0^k(r); q = exp_0^k(c)
  w = mobius_add(-q, p, k); nw = ||w||
  if nw < 1e-8: u = v / nv
  else: u = w / nw
  return nv * u
Curvature pseudocode (no_grad, every 100 epochs):
  for l in 1..3: A_l = quotient(W, prefix_map[l-1])
  kappa_raw[l] = weighted_mean(ollivier_ricci(A_l), weights=transition_counts)
  for b in 1..10: A_l^null = null(A_l, mode=l); kappa_null[l,b] = same(A_l^null)
  mu[l] = mean_b kappa_null[l,b]; sigma[l] = std_b kappa_null[l,b]
  z[l] = clip((kappa_raw[l]-mu[l])/max(sigma[l],1e-6), -3, 3)
  m[l] = median over training items of ||r_l - c_l||
  k_ref[l] = 1/m[l]^2
  b[l] = z[1] - z[l]
  kappa[l] = clip(k_ref[l]*exp(b[l]/2), 0.22*k_ref[l], 4.48*k_ref[l])
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: r_l (batch x d) Euclidean residual entering level l, chosen code c_l (batch x d), scalar kappa_l, epsilon=1e-8. Output: r_{l+1} (batch x d) with ||r_{l+1}|| = ||r_l - c_l|| exactly, plus the unchanged integer codes and SID tokens. The curvature schedule takes the training transition matrix, the training item-to-prefix map and the current codebook, and returns the detached vector (kappa_1, kappa_2, kappa_3).

specification.text: Notation: ball B_k = {x : k||x||^2 < 1}, Mobius addition x (+) y = ((1 + 2k<x,y> + k||y||^2)x + (1-k||x||^2)y) / (1 + 2k<x,y> + k^2||x||^2||y||^2), exp_0^k(v) = tanh(sqrt(k)||v||) v/(sqrt(k)||v||), log_0^k its inverse. Residual operator bend_k(r,c): v = r-c; if ||v|| < eps return 0; p = exp_0^k(r); q = exp_0^k(c); w = (-q) (+) p; if ||w|| < eps return ||v|| v/||v||; return ||v|| w/||w||. As k -> 0, exp_0 -> id and (+) -> +, so w -> v and the operator returns exactly v. Curvature schedule every 100 epochs, detached, training split only: build the item transition graph W; for l=1,2,3 map training items to their current level-(l-1) prefix (level 1 = item itself), sum W over prefix pairs to obtain quotient adjacency A_l, compute edge Ollivier-Ricci curvature with a lazy random walk and Wasserstein-1, take the transition-count-weighted mean kappa_raw,l, standardise against B=10 size-preserving nulls (level 1: degree-preserving stub rewiring of W; levels 2,3: shuffle item-to-prefix membership preserving prefix sizes), z_l = clip((kappa_raw,l - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, -3, +3). Then b_l = z_1 - z_l, k_ref,l = 1/m_l^2 with m_l the median training residual norm ||r_l - c_l|| at the previous recompute, and kappa_l = clip(k_ref,l * exp(b_l/2), 0.22*k_ref,l, 4.48*k_ref,l). For l=2,3 set r_l <- bend_{kappa_l}(r_{l-1}, c_{l-1}) before the level-l nearest-code search; level 1 uses r_1 = z unchanged. The three switches are constructor flags: BEHAVIOUR_OFF sets z_l = 0 for all l (flat profile, kappa_l = k_ref,l, geometry still active); GEOMETRY_OFF sets kappa_l = 0 exactly (exp_0 = id, (+) = +, residual = r_l - c_l, Euclidean RQ); both on uses the real z_l. No arm is trained in this round; the flags exist only so the coupling can be audited.

ideas.title: Resolution-safe behaviour-curvature bending of the RQ residual direction

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
